label: Vector Bundles
notes: This chapter covers printed pages 249 through 271 and introduces vector bundles as smoothly varying families of vector spaces over a base manifold. The governing question all chapter is which data are fiberwise linear, which are merely smooth, and which local choices glue consistently across overlapping charts.

label: Definition of a Vector Bundle
notes: A vector bundle bundles a vector space onto each base point and demands local product structure. Stress the three pieces students forget: the projection is surjective and submersive, fibers carry a fixed dimension, and every local trivialization is fiberwise a linear isomorphism onto the model space.

label: Local Trivializations
notes: A local trivialization is a coordinate system for fibers. Over a neighborhood the bundle looks exactly like a product, with the trivialization recording each vector's components. Emphasize that triviality is always available locally; the whole subject is about what survives when you try to extend it globally.

label: Transition Functions and the Cocycle
notes: Transition functions compare two trivializations on an overlap and take values in the general linear group. Walk through the cocycle identity slowly: it is the consistency condition guaranteeing that pairwise gluings agree on triple overlaps, and it is exactly the data needed to rebuild a bundle from charts.

label: The Bundle Construction Lemma
notes: This lemma is the converse engine of the chapter. Given an open cover and smooth maps into the general linear group satisfying the cocycle condition, you can assemble a genuine smooth vector bundle. Point out that almost every bundle in later chapters is built precisely this way, from transition data.

label: The Tangent Bundle
notes: The tangent bundle is the chapter's flagship example. A coordinate chart hands you a local frame of coordinate vector fields, the frame gives the trivialization, and the change-of-coordinates Jacobian is the transition function. Make sure students see that smoothness of the bundle follows directly from smoothness of chart overlaps.

label: The Cotangent Bundle
notes: The cotangent bundle dualizes every fiber. A covector is a linear test applied to tangent vectors, and the dual coframe is verified by a pairing matrix that must come out as the identity. Highlight the contravariant transition law: cotangent transitions use the inverse transpose Jacobian, reversing the tangent rule.

label: Trivial Bundle vs Mobius Band
notes: Here is the heart of the chapter. The product line bundle over the circle closes up into a cylinder, but the Mobius band returns its fiber direction with a sign flip. Stress that both look identical over any short arc; the twist lives only in how the global return is recorded.

label: Sections and the Module of Sections
notes: A section picks one vector in each fiber, smoothly. The set of smooth sections forms a module over the ring of smooth functions, since you can scale a section pointwise by any smooth function. This module viewpoint is the algebraic backbone for everything that follows in the course.

label: Local and Global Frames
notes: A local frame is a trivialization rewritten in section language: independent sections forming a basis in every fiber. A global frame is equivalent to a global trivialization. For a line bundle, a nowhere-zero global section already is a global frame, which is why the Mobius forced zero obstructs triviality.

label: Bundle Homomorphisms
notes: A bundle homomorphism acts fiber by fiber as a smoothly varying matrix. The key lemma characterizes such maps as exactly the smooth-function-linear operations on sections. Multiplication by a smooth function passes this test; differentiation fails it, which is the cleanest way to separate tensorial maps from differential operators.

label: Subbundles
notes: A subbundle is a constant-rank family of subspaces that assembles smoothly. The practical test is the local frame criterion: near each point you must find smooth sections spanning the proposed subspaces. The radial line field vanishing at the origin is the canonical failure, where rank drops and the subbundle condition collapses.

label: Fiber Bundles and Recap
notes: Fiber bundles keep the local product diagram but drop the requirement that fibers be vector spaces with linear transitions. A two-sheet cover and the interval Mobius band illustrate non-linear model fibers. Close by recapping the throughline: local product, global gluing, and sections as the visible test of triviality.
